references: Native SRT1.5.3 Broadcast fixed720p1800kbps, buffer120ms, peer-idle60s
fault: A down/up, then C down/up, then B down/up; one100% bidirectional packet blackhole at a time; interfaces remain UP
limitations: Controlled pilot, not statistical superiority or physical-radio validation
Three steps generated inside developer bounds; benchmark keeps previous profiles; protocol/security/priority unchanged
Shaping caps are settings, not independently rerun capacity calibration
Two adaptive encoders/decoders versus one each for fixed SRT references
Light timing and full image-fidelity runs are separate; do not pool CPU/timing
Low-path delays are not a bandwidth oracle; high promotion tests actual receiver delivery
High selection may change before a fault; report observed route rather than claim a switch
Synthetic source to decoded availability, not glass-to-glass; sampled blockSSIM not VMAF
Different resolution policies; no equal-image-quality claim
SRT120ms is this reference configuration, not fastest possible SRT; no universal transport superiority claim
Two balanced repetitions are a short repeatability check, not a statistical significance test
Short packet blackholes, not physical carrier failure or long socket expiration
primary_goal: Lower time-weighted lag behind newest capture, including silence; dropped old frames are not failures
